Exercise: Standing One-Arm Cable Curl

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- elbow_flexion

Primary Muscles:

- biceps

Secondary Muscles:
None

Equipment:

- cable

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: Recent bicep injury, reason: May exacerbate existing injuries
- condition: Shoulder instability, reason: Can increase risk of shoulder strain or dislocation

Exercise Variations:

- name: Concentration Curl, description: Perform the exercise with one arm resting on a bench for added focus and isolation.
- name: Hammer Curl, description: Hold the cable handle with an underhand grip to target the brachialis muscle.

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Barbell Curl, equipment: barbell
- exercise_name: Dumbbell Curl, equipment: dumbbells

Instructions:

- Start out by grabbing single handle next to the low pulley machine. Make sure you are far enough from the machine so that your arm is supporting the weight.
- Make sure that your upper arm is stationary, perpendicular to the floor with elbows in and palms facing forward. Your non lifting arm should be grabbing your waist. This will allow you to keep your balance.
- Slowly begin to curl the single handle upwards while keeping the upper arm stationary until your forearm touches your bicep while exhaling. Tip: Only the forearm should move.
- Hold the contraction position as you squeeze the bicep and then lower the single handle back down to the starting position as you inhale.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
- Switch arms while performing this exercise.
